items.summary: West Africa's central bank has doubled the amount customers can hold in mobile money wallets to FCFA 4 million ($6,850), while raising monthly top-up limits and relaxing rules on how issuers manage customer funds. The changes, which take effect on November 2, could make mobile wallets more useful for small businesses and households, give fintechs more opportunities to earn from customer funds, and increase competition with banks and microfinance institutions. But allowing issuers to hold a smaller share of those funds in readily accessible deposits also raises questions about liquidity, customer protection and regulatory oversight.
